title: Assessing the Physical Sensitivity of Water Systems to Low Flow and Drought, Through Response Scenarios Under the Neutral Approach in a Water Resource Management Context
content: The ultimate goal of climate change adaptation in the context of water resources management is undoubtedly to anticipate the conditions that water systems will face due to changes in climate dynamics and act accordingly. This can be achieved through an exploratory analysis of classified target sector scenarios adapted to the decision context and based on integrating the concepts of the main axes of water resources management, disaster risk management and climate change adaptation. This study is framed in an informed and contextualized potential impact assessment process of the physical sensibility to climate change on low flows and droughts in 6 catchments in Quebec (Canada), using the neutral scenario method that imbricates both bottom-up and top-down approaches. Valuable insights are gained on the potential behavior of low flows and droughts, which have been studied little in this region. The results show an uncorrelated behavior between low flows and droughts and the particularity of the response of each catchment to the same climatic changes. Special emphasis was placed on synthesizing the large volume of results to present them with a clear division between the information generated “about” and “for” climate change adaptation. In addition to contributing to hydrological research, the approach adopted here is also routed into the decision support system, aiming to operationalize risk assessment and make water resources management more efficient.
